thread:
sara: Hey runtime — small, auditable benchmark pack request for the launch post. Need a compact artifact set + a short methodology note legal can review. Keep it reproducible and no cherry-picking.

jules: Which model and sample cohort? Also want reproducible seed so auditors can rerun.

sara: Use model: "redwood-x-7b-alpha" (the one in the landing draft). Use cohort: marketing_cohort_final. Sampling seed=31415. Include sample IDs in samples_manifest.json and md5s for the payload files.

marc: For warmup distribution we’ll do linear ramp + poisson jitter per request generator. Confirm that warmup sessions should be independent (no shared session) — marketing wants that to reflect multi-tenant traffic.

sara: Yes — independent sessions for warmup. For long-context tests include both independent requests and a follow-on request to exercise a warm KV cache.

leo: Plan: schedule three jobs on pool-5: job-warmup-21111, job-cold-21112, job-quant-21113. Upload artifacts to s3://internal-bench/marketing/1815554321/. We'll add md5 checksums and a SHA256 of the run metadata. ETA 20-36h.

jules: Product wants a single PNG for the post (warmup_share.png) and a tiny time-series CSV for reproducibility. Legal also asked for a 1-paragraph caveat in the methodology_note.txt about sample representativeness.

legal-bot: Reminder: methodology_note.txt must include sample provenance (cohort path, seed), full run commands, infra details (instance type, CUDA and driver), and a plain-language claim mapped to the p95 in claim_snippet.md. Also ensure artifacts are embargoed until launch week.

leo: Example curl command we will put verbatim (token redacted):

```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-x-7b-alpha","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<sample>"}],"max_tokens":1024,"stream":false,"cache_kv":false}'
```

leo: We will also include the exact launch flags and kernel settings used (e.g., mkldnn off, use_fast_attention=true) in runbook metadata and mark any non-default flags as EXPERIMENTAL.

marc: For quant runs we'll capture peak GPU memory and failure modes. If q5_0 is unstable we'll capture fallback latency numbers on q4_0 and include a one-line explanation in claim_snippet.md.

jules: Can you add a tiny reproducibility snippet in the manifest that contains the curl + seed + path to samples so someone can rerun locally? That's critical for legal.

leo: Yes — samples_manifest.json will include: cohort path, seed, list of sample IDs, md5 of payload and of artifact_pack.tar.gz. We'll push artifacts and md5+sha256 checksums.txt to the S3 folder and paste links here.

sara: Embargo until launch week. Mark anything preliminary or experimental in the manifest clearly. If you can provide a warmup_preview.png (1k requests) by EOD that would help copy review.

leo: ETA for preview: ~6h. ETA for full artifacts: 20-36h. Initial job ids posted to logs: https://internal.redwood/bench/runs/21111. Tagging plan: I will @jules @sara @marc when artifacts are uploaded.

runtime-bot: job-warmup-21111 queued on pool-5 (est runtime ~90m). job-cold-21112 queued. job-quant-21113 queued. Artifacts target: s3://internal-bench/marketing/1815554321/. Notification will be posted on completion.

marc: Thanks — and please call out any >10% perf regression for quant variants vs fp16 in the quant_summary.csv and in claim_snippet.md so product/legal can evaluate.

jules: One last note: avoid any curated selection language in the blog. We'll rely on the sample manifest + seed to demonstrate non-curation.

sara: Perfect. Thanks team — looking forward to the preview and the final artifact_pack.tar.gz.

leo: Copy that. Will update here with S3 links + checksums when ready.
